clue.text: Cultivates grass in manure initially?

indicators.note: in places the plant word inside the letters drawn from the manure word
initially points to the opening letters of a phrase, read as its abbreviation

parts.note: manure is crudely 'bull shit', and its initial letters are B and S; this is the first
a reed is a tall grass
the second initial of 'bull shit'

explanation.surface: A gardener tends grass by working manure into it first.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the cheeky reading of manure as 'bull shit', whose initials BS go round the grass.
explanation.definitionFit: To breed plants or animals is to raise and cultivate them, a direct verb synonym.

clue.text: Terribly drab old PM who's had many rôles

indicators.note: terribly suggests something done badly, so these letters are jumbled out of order

parts.note: the four letters to be rearranged
William Pitt, father and son, were eighteenth-century British prime ministers

explanation.surface: A dull former prime minister has played many parts in his career.
explanation.walkthrough: Pitt the Younger and Pitt the Elder were both British prime ministers; the definition describes the Hollywood star as one who has acted many roles.
explanation.definitionFit: Brad Pitt is a film actor with a long career of screen parts, so he is someone who has had many roles.

clue.text: Advanced years, when Thatcher was in her prime?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the ages from eighty to eighty-nine

definitions.text: when Thatcher was in her prime
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the decade from 1980, when Margaret Thatcher was at the height of her power

explanation.surface: An old person's age, and the era of Margaret Thatcher's prime.
explanation.walkthrough: Margaret Thatcher was UK prime minister from 1979 to 1990, so the decade fits; the question mark marks the playful second definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a span of a person's old age and the decade of the 1980s.

clue.text: Leading doctors envisage large health investment for city

indicators.note: leading points to the front letter of each of the following words

parts.note: the first letters of these five words

explanation.surface: Senior doctors plan a big spend on healthcare for a city.
explanation.definitionFit: Delhi is the major Indian city containing the capital, New Delhi.

clue.text: Headcase swaps sides — it's something of a cliché

indicators.note: swaps sides tells you to move the back half of the compound to the front, rotating the letters round

parts.note: split into head and case: nut is slang for the head, and a chest is a case or box

explanation.surface: A crazy person's behaviour seems a hackneyed routine.
explanation.walkthrough: Headcase reads as a slang word for a madman, but it splits into head and case, whose synonyms are then swapped round.
explanation.definitionFit: An old chestnut is a stale joke or story repeated too often, much like a cliché.

clue.text: No one has birth as complicated as he imagined!

definitions.text: No one has birth as complicated as he imagined!

indicators.note: complicated means tangled up, so the letters are twisted into a new order

parts.note: the thirteen letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Nobody's birth could be as convoluted as the one this man dreamt up.
explanation.walkthrough: W. Heath Robinson was a British cartoonist famed for drawing absurdly complicated contraptions; his name became a byword for them.
explanation.definitionFit: The cartoonist drew ludicrously elaborate machines, so the whole clue describes him as a man who imagined complication.

clue.text: Fantastic medical support includes recreational space

indicators.note: includes means one thing holds another, so the support word wraps round the space word

parts.note: a sling supports an injured arm
a park is open ground for recreation

explanation.surface: A splendid hospital brace somehow contains a playground.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparkling performance means brilliant or dazzling, so it serves as a synonym of fantastic.

clue.text: Almost make out with sailor that's so sweet

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to neck is to kiss and cuddle, to make out
tar is an old word for a sailor

explanation.surface: Nearly getting off with a seaman sounds rather sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a phrase describing a substance: nectar is the stuff that is so sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: Nectar is the sugary liquid of flowers and the drink of the gods, proverbially delicious.

clue.text: Belief is part of those who traditionally oppose us

indicators.note: part of puts the short word among the letters of the longer phrase's synonym

parts.note: 'us and them' is the traditional opposition of one side to the other
taken as written

explanation.surface: A faith that sets itself against our side.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'us and them' makes the long description mean the other side, THEM, which holds IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Theism is belief in a god or gods, so it is a kind of religious belief.

clue.text: Work together on article depicting financial investor

indicators.note: on in an across clue places the first word's synonym after the second

parts.note: an indefinite article
a team gels when it works together well

explanation.surface: A piece of writing about collaboration portrays a backer.
explanation.definitionFit: An angel is a private backer who puts money into a show or a start-up business.

clue.text: Suffer naval disruption getting stuck inside deluge

indicators.note: getting stuck inside means lodged within, so the rearranged letters go inside the verb
disruption throws things into disorder, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the five letters of naval rearranged
the rest of ache, after the insertion
to ache is to suffer; its first letter comes before the insertion

explanation.surface: A navy suffers disorder after getting stranded in a flood.
explanation.walkthrough: ACHE is suffer, split around the shuffled letters of naval.
explanation.definitionFit: An avalanche is an overwhelming mass, just as a deluge is an overwhelming flood of something.

clue.text: Handsome pupil perhaps

definitions.note: the answer is a noun phrase for a good-looking person, while handsome is an adjective

definitions.meaning: second meaning, read literally: a pupil is a small part of an eye, an organ for looking

explanation.walkthrough: Pupil suggests a schoolchild, but it is the opening of the eye, one bit of a 'looker'.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone a bit of a looker means they are quite attractive, close to handsome.

clue.text: Culture has potential for growth here?

definitions.text: Culture has potential for growth here?

parts.words: Culture has potential for growth here?
parts.note: surface reading: a society or the arts with room to develop
setter's reading: a bacterial culture growing in the laboratory vessel used for it

explanation.walkthrough: Culture reads as arts or society, but it means microbes grown in a lab.
explanation.definitionFit: A shallow lidded glass plate is where scientists grow bacterial cultures.

clue.text: King takes in poet

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
to take in food is to eat

explanation.surface: A monarch receives a visiting poet.
explanation.definitionFit: John Keats was an English Romantic poet, so he is an example of a poet.

clue.text: Victor expelled from crumbling private school somewhere in Greece

parts.note: V is Victor in the phonetic alphabet
the letters to be reworked once the V goes

explanation.surface: A boy named Victor is expelled from a decaying private school.
explanation.definitionFit: The Acropolis is the ancient citadel above Athens, a famous location in Greece.

clue.text: Being humble, turned up to return lost headgear

definitions.meaning: first meaning: approaching someone humbly, as when asking a favour

definitions.text: turned up to return lost headgear
definitions.meaning: second meaning, read literally: a hat held ready in the hand by someone who has come to give it back

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a playful literal picture: someone arrives holding a lost hat to return it.
explanation.definitionFit: To come cap in hand is to ask meekly and deferentially, as a supplicant would.

clue.text: One has trouble getting into them — they're difficult to read

definitions.text: One has trouble getting into them
definitions.meaning: first meaning: being in someone's ... means being in disfavour, in trouble
second meaning, read literally: poorly written volumes are hard going

explanation.walkthrough: Getting into a book sounds like becoming absorbed in it, but here it is landing in disfavour.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'in someone's bad books' means out of favour, and literally poor novels are tough to read.

clue.text: Eight fallen over — it takes forever to understand its meaning

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a figure 8 lying on its side is the infinity sign, the symbol of endless time
second meaning: a plain synonym, the word needed to explain the answer's meaning

explanation.walkthrough: An 8 lying on its side is the infinity sign; the rest of the clue says that the word forever is what you need to explain its meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Eternity is endless time, symbolised by the sideways-eight sign and glossed as forever.

clue.text: It lets you have a say on boards?

definitions.text: It lets you have a say on boards?

parts.words: It lets you have a say on boards?
parts.note: surface reading: a seat on a company board giving a voice in decisions
setter's reading: the boards are the stage, and the role lets an actor deliver lines

explanation.walkthrough: Boards suggests company directors, but 'the boards' is the theatre stage.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor given a role with lines, rather than a walk-on, gets to say something on stage.

clue.text: Huge amount of slime on backed-up register

indicators.note: backed-up in a down clue means read from the bottom up, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: a log is a record or register

explanation.definitionFit: A googol is ten to the power one hundred, an enormous number.

parts.note: working is ON, and double means take it twice
I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: Two people working on an island hunt for something to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: An onion is a bulb vegetable used in cooking, so it is one kind of food.

clue.text: Tory sabre rattling in upmarket diner

parts.note: the nine letters to be rearranged; a Tory is a British Conservative

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician makes threats in a smart restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: Sabre rattling is an idiom for making threats, which hides the shuffle signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An oyster bar serves shellfish and is typically pricey, so it is a smart eating place.

parts.note: Brussels is the seat of the European Union

taken as written
